summary: A country-themed section within Royal Park Rajapruek in Mae Hia, southwest of Chiang Mai. The park lists 22 international gardens representing 21 countries, alongside Thai and horticultural displays across more than 500 rai. Treat the gardens as part of a large outdoor park visit; their current planting and upkeep can vary.
whyGo: Compare garden designs and country references in one easy-to-follow themed area.
Combine the international gardens with Ho Kham Luang, orchid and flower houses, or other park zones for a varied half-day outing.
The Bhutan garden offers a distinct Himalayan-style setting and is one example of the international section.
The park is a relaxed choice for garden photography and time outdoors away from the Old City.
bestFor: Visitors interested in landscape design, plants and themed gardens
Photography, families and an unhurried outdoor half-day
Travelers pairing several park attractions in one visit
skipIf: You only have a short window and want a compact attraction in central Chiang Mai
You expect each international garden to be a fully maintained or detailed cultural exhibit; current condition and interpretation were not verified
You need a fully indoor or guaranteed step-free experience
duration: Allow 2–4 hours for selected park areas as a planning estimate; seeing the international gardens alongside other displays can take longer. The grounds are extensive, so use the park tram to reduce walking and choose priorities on arrival.
cost: The official admission page lists foreign adults at THB 200 and children 100–140 cm at THB 150; children under 100 cm enter free. The official park FAQ says the sightseeing tram is free. Rates may change before December 2026; transport to the park, food and any rentals are extra.
hours: The park lists daily hours of 08:00–18:00. Allow time to reach the international section and return before closing; check official notices for temporary closures or altered event hours.
bestTime: Arrive near opening or from about 15:00 for cooler walking and softer photography light. December is within Chiang Mai’s cooler season, but exact garden displays and bloom timing vary.
gettingThere: The park is in Mae Hia, southwest of central Chiang Mai. A taxi, ride-hail car or hired driver is the simplest plan; arrange a return ride. The Tourism Authority of Thailand gives approaches via Canal Road/Highway 121 or Chiang Mai–Hang Dong Road/Highway 108, then Ratchaphruek Road. Public transit service was not confirmed.
booking: No advance booking requirement for ordinary park entry was found; the official admission page presents standard ticket rates. Check the park website close to your date for current tickets, event arrangements and temporary garden closures.
accessibility: This is a large outdoor site with distances between displays. The official admission page says visitors with disabilities enter free; the park map marks accessible parking and some ramps, and a free tram can reduce walking. Step-free access across every international garden, tram boarding details and accessible toilets were not confirmed; contact the park about specific requirements.
practicalTips: Check the official map at entry and select a few country gardens rather than trying to cover the whole park on foot.
Confirm that the particular international gardens you most want to see are open and in good condition; no garden-by-garden December schedule was found.
Bring water, sun protection and comfortable shoes for outdoor paths.
Use the free tram to shorten distances, then walk through the garden section at your own pace.
decemberNotes: December is a popular cool-season time to visit Chiang Mai, and Rajapruek’s annual Flora Festival has run in past December seasons. The park’s 2026 notice confirms preparation works in August and September 2026, but the sources reviewed do not confirm December 2026 festival dates, evening hours or a programme for the international gardens. Plan around standard 08:00–18:00 park hours and check official updates near the trip.
uncertainties: The number and names of gardens are listed by the official park, but their current presentation, maintenance and any temporary access restrictions were not confirmed individually.
December 2026 Flora Festival dates, special displays, evening opening and event prices remain unverified.
Flower displays vary with planting and weather; specific blooms cannot be guaranteed.
Admission prices and vehicle arrangements may change before the visit; comprehensive step-free access details were unavailable.
